```json
{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Use Spring Boot 1.x with Spring XD as the baseline for the XD-related user stories (U1, U2) since they target XD's composed job model.",
    "Reuse the existing Composed Job / Partitioned Job domain model in Spring XD; introduce an AggregatedProgressCalculator that aggregates leaf job progress events published via the existing deployment manifest / job listener infrastructure rather than introducing a new event bus.",
    "For composed job restart (U2), persist composed job execution state (step status, partition map, parent job instance id) in the existing relational job repository so re-launch can reuse the same instance topology.",
    "Kafka 0.9 investigation (U3) is scoped to a spike: produce a written report plus a minimal proof-of-concept binding using the new 0.9 producer/consumer APIs; no production refactor is included in this increment.",
    "For Lattice bootstrap (U4), target the Lattice CLI + Diego brain and provide a bash-based bootstrapper (similar in style to existing Cloud Foundry bootstrap) that wires the s-c-d server and Skipper into a Lattice cell on bare metal.",
    "For the dot-delimited property syntax in spring-cloud-stream (U5), implement a SpEL/DotResolver in the binding's property resolver chain so that both Tuple and JSON payloads can reference nested properties (e.g., 'foo.bar[0].baz').",
    "Tab completion (U6) is implemented in the spring-cloud-dataflow-shell (CLI based on spring-shell) by exposing a CompletionProvider that introspects the registered modules/options DSL and reuses JLine's candidate completion API.",
    "For Mesos deployment (U7), target the Marathon framework on Mesos and provide a deployer module that translates s-c-d App/Stream definitions into Marathon application groups; treat DCOS as out of scope.",
    "For the redis @Rule move (U8), extract the rule into a new module s-c-d-test-fixtures-redis published as a separate artifact and rewrite consumers (stream applications tests) to depend on the new artifact.",
    "Testing strategy: JUnit + Spring Test for unit/integration, end-to-end smoke tests for shell tab completion and Mesos/Lattice bootstrap are scripted but executed manually because no CI infrastructure is in scope for this increment."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "A single experienced Java/Spring developer (the estimator) is performing all the work; no team coordination overhead is added beyond a small integration buffer.",
    "Effort is expressed in work-hours of focused development time (no meetings, no context switching overhead beyond a modest integration/test buffer).",
    "The starting codebase is a stable snapshot of Spring XD / spring-cloud-dataflow compatible with the Spring 4.x / Spring Boot 1.x line at the time these stories were filed.",
    "No new infrastructure (CI, artifact repository, Mesos cluster) needs to be provisioned as part of this increment; Lattice/Mesos work assumes a developer can spin up local clusters for testing.",
    "Kafka 0.9 work is investigation-only with a small PoC; a full upgrade to Kafka 0.9 is excluded from this increment.",
    "Redis @Rule extraction is purely a code-organization/refactoring change; no behavioral changes are made to the rule itself.",
    "Documentation is limited to inline Javadoc, a short README per new module/repo, and the investigation report for U3; a full user-guide rewrite is excluded.",
    "Code review and merge overhead is implicitly included in each per-story estimate and is not broken out as a separate activity."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Architecture and design",
      "activity_description": "Read the existing XD / s-c-d / spring-cloud-stream code to understand the composed job, deployment, and shell architectures. Produce a short design note covering: progress aggregation model, restart semantics, dot-resolver extension point, tab completion data model, and the Lattice/Mesos deployer interfaces. Resolve cross-cutting decisions (e.g., which GitHub org/repo the redis fixtures move to, naming conventions).",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "U1 - Aggregated progress bar for composed jobs",
      "activity_description": "Implement an AggregatedProgressCalculator that listens to leaf job/step progress events from the existing job event bus, computes weighted aggregated percentages, and exposes them via the JobExecutionResource REST endpoint and the XD Shell 'job display' command. Includes unit tests for the calculator and an integration test for a parent job with two embedded child jobs.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "U2 - Restart an existing composed job",
      "activity_description": "Persist composed job topology (parent JobInstance + child JobInstances + partition map) in the relational job repository. Add a 'job restart' REST endpoint and a 'job restart' shell command that re-launches a previously failed/composed job, reusing the original step/partition layout. Includes state-validation logic and integration tests covering partial failure and re-completion scenarios.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "U3 - Kafka 0.9 integration investigation (spike)",
      "activity_description": "Spike to investigate the Kafka 0.9 release: new producer/consumer API surface, security features (SSL/SASL), and implications for spring-kafka and spring-cloud-stream binders used by s-c-d. Deliverables: an investigation report listing integration touch points, breaking changes, and improvement areas, plus a small PoC branch demonstrating a 0.9 producer/consumer against an embedded broker.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "U4 - Lattice bootstrap for bare metal deployment",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement a Lattice bootstrapper (bash scripts + a small Java launcher) that: configures a Lattice cell on a bare-metal host (Diego brain + receptor + cell), deploys the s-c-d server and Skipper as Lattice applications, and wires their environment to point at the cell. Includes a smoke-test script that deploys a sample stream and verifies it is running.",
      "most_likely_effort": 28
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "U5 - Dot-delimited property resolution in spring-cloud-stream",
      "activity_description": "Extend the spring-cloud-stream binding property resolver to support a dot-delimited syntax (e.g., 'foo.bar[0].baz') for both Tuple and JSON payload property references. Implement a DotPathResolver used by the binding's PropertyResolver chain, with support for indexed access on collections. Includes unit tests covering nested objects, collections, and mixed Tuple/JSON payloads.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "U6 - Tab completion in s-c-d shell",
      "activity_description": "Add tab completion to the spring-cloud-dataflow-shell CLI. Implement a CompletionProvider that exposes module names, stream/task definitions, command options, and runtime hints. Hook it into JLine's candidate completion for the relevant commands. Includes unit tests for the provider and a manual end-to-end verification of completion behavior for 'stream create', 'task launch', and module definition syntax.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "U7 - Deploy s-c-d on Mesos",
      "activity_description": "Implement a Mesos deployer that translates s-c-d Stream/Task/App definitions into Marathon application groups and deploys them to a Mesos cluster. Includes: a Deployer SPI implementation, Marathon REST client integration, support for stream scaling via Marathon instance counts, and a manual smoke test that deploys a sample stream on a local Mesos/Marathon setup and verifies the apps reach RUNNING state.",
      "most_likely_effort": 36
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "U8 - Move redis @Rule to a separate repo",
      "activity_description": "Extract the @Rule-based redis test fixture (used in stream application tests) from the s-c-d core repo into a new repo/artifact (e.g., spring-cloud-dataflow-test-fixtures-redis). Create the new Gradle/Maven build, set up CI-friendly POM, and update all in-repo consumers to depend on the new artifact. Verify that the existing test suite still passes after the extraction.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Integration and end-to-end testing",
      "activity_description": "Cross-feature integration pass: run the full s-c-d test suite with all the above changes applied; execute the Lattice and Mesos smoke tests; manually exercise the XD Shell to confirm composed job progress display, restart, and tab completion work together; fix any regressions uncovered.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Documentation",
      "activity_description": "Update inline Javadoc, write a README for the new redis fixtures artifact, document the Lattice and Mesos bootstrap/deployment steps in a short 'Platforms' section, publish the Kafka 0.9 investigation report, and add release notes entries for U1, U2, U5, U6, U7, and U8.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 236
  }
}
```

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot 1.x with Spring XD as the baseline for the XD-related user stories (U1, U2) since they target XD's composed job model.

Reuse the existing Composed Job / Partitioned Job domain model in Spring XD; introduce an AggregatedProgressCalculator that aggregates leaf job progress events published via the existing deployment manifest / job listener infrastructure rather than introducing a new event bus.

For composed job restart (U2), persist composed job execution state (step status, partition map, parent job instance id) in the existing relational job repository so re-launch can reuse the same instance topology.

Kafka 0.9 investigation (U3) is scoped to a spike: produce a written report plus a minimal proof-of-concept binding using the new 0.9 producer/consumer APIs; no production refactor is included in this increment.

For Lattice bootstrap (U4), target the Lattice CLI + Diego brain and provide a bash-based bootstrapper (similar in style to existing Cloud Foundry bootstrap) that wires the s-c-d server and Skipper into a Lattice cell on bare metal.

For the dot-delimited property syntax in spring-cloud-stream (U5), implement a SpEL/DotResolver in the binding's property resolver chain so that both Tuple and JSON payloads can reference nested properties (e.g., 'foo.bar[0].baz').

Tab completion (U6) is implemented in the spring-cloud-dataflow-shell (CLI based on spring-shell) by exposing a CompletionProvider that introspects the registered modules/options DSL and reuses JLine's candidate completion API.

For Mesos deployment (U7), target the Marathon framework on Mesos and provide a deployer module that translates s-c-d App/Stream definitions into Marathon application groups; treat DCOS as out of scope.

For the redis @Rule move (U8), extract the rule into a new module s-c-d-test-fixtures-redis published as a separate artifact and rewrite consumers (stream applications tests) to depend on the new artifact.

Testing strategy: JUnit + Spring Test for unit/integration, end-to-end smoke tests for shell tab completion and Mesos/Lattice bootstrap are scripted but executed manually because no CI infrastructure is in scope for this increment.
assumptions: A single experienced Java/Spring developer (the estimator) is performing all the work; no team coordination overhead is added beyond a small integration buffer.
Effort is expressed in work-hours of focused development time (no meetings, no context switching overhead beyond a modest integration/test buffer).
The starting codebase is a stable snapshot of Spring XD / spring-cloud-dataflow compatible with the Spring 4.x / Spring Boot 1.x line at the time these stories were filed.
No new infrastructure (CI, artifact repository, Mesos cluster) needs to be provisioned as part of this increment; Lattice/Mesos work assumes a developer can spin up local clusters for testing.
Kafka 0.9 work is investigation-only with a small PoC; a full upgrade to Kafka 0.9 is excluded from this increment.
Redis @Rule extraction is purely a code-organization/refactoring change; no behavioral changes are made to the rule itself.
Documentation is limited to inline Javadoc, a short README per new module/repo, and the investigation report for U3; a full user-guide rewrite is excluded.
Code review and merge overhead is implicitly included in each per-story estimate and is not broken out as a separate activity.
